escalations.one_line: Variable uses the synthesized decoder, so a stored variable object missing isSecret throws keyNotFound, the throw escapes decodeIfPresent, and the outer try? silently drops every custom server.
criteria: C4 - silent data loss the user cannot detect or undo: one malformed nested object discards the entire custom-server list with no message (the try? at MCPStore.swift:247), and the first subsequent edit atomically overwrites mcp-customs.json with the empty list (MCPStore.swift:275). No backup, no undo, and nothing tells the user their file failed to parse.
escalations.worst: A user with a hand-edited or partially corrupted mcp-customs.json - the exact case the file's own doc comment says is tolerated - opens the app and finds Settings > MCP > Custom empty, with no error anywhere. If they then add a replacement server, saveCustoms atomically overwrites the file with the single new entry and every previous custom server definition (name, command, args, url, variable keys) is permanently gone. Keychain secrets are NOT destroyed on this path, since deleteCustom is never called, so they survive as orphans - this is lost configuration, retypeable, not lost credentials and not lost project work. Probability is low: isSecret has existed since the file's first commit (75e30f217, 2026-09-18), so no shipped build ever wrote a Variable without it, and the trigger is an out-of-band edit or file corruption.

escalations.one_line: The custom-server ellipsis menu's Delete calls model.mcp.deleteCustom(server) on one click with no confirmation, ignoring settings.confirmBeforeDeleting, and deleteCustom also runs disconnect(), which deletes the server's Keychain secrets.
criteria: C2: deleteCustom calls disconnect(), whose first act is MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry) at MCPStore.swift:124. The server's stored API keys and other secret variable values are erased from the Keychain. For an OAuth entry, MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID:) at :126 also discards the stored grant. The app offers no recovery path; the user must re-obtain each credential from the vendor.

C1: the custom server definition itself (command, args, URL, plain variable values) is removed from the customs list at :197 and written out by saveCustoms() at :198, so the user's own configuration is destroyed in the same click.

C5: settings.confirmBeforeDeleting defaults to true (AppSettings.swift:702, key at :123, setter at :209-210) and is honored by six other destructive paths (SettingsView.swift:851, :892; SidebarView.swift:192, :360, :891). This one path overrides the user's explicit safety preference.
escalations.worst: A single mis-aimed click in a small ellipsis menu, on a row immediately below a Disconnect entry, permanently erases a custom MCP server's configuration and its Keychain secrets with no prompt and no undo, even for a user who has explicitly asked to be asked before deleting. Recovery requires re-obtaining every credential from the upstream vendor and re-entering the server by hand.

escalations.one_line: The cookie-timeout tearDown deletes the shared scratch index while another caller's detached capture may be using it, the exact hazard the registry-eviction path documents and avoids.
criteria: C1: a revert against a silently truncated checkpoint deletes files at Git.swift:619 whose pre-turn, uncommitted content exists nowhere else, so the user's work is permanently lost.
C4: the truncated capture exits 0 and is cached and committed as an ordinary checkpoint, so neither app nor user can tell the snapshot is wrong until a revert acts on it.
escalations.worst: Usually benign: the turn simply has no checkpoint and the user later sees "No file checkpoint is available for this message." The bad outcome, which the source itself names, is a checkpoint that silently records only a few directories as though it were the whole tree. A later revert against that base then treats every other touched file as new (Git.swift:613) and DELETES it with FileManager.removeItem (Git.swift:619) instead of restoring its pre-turn content; for an uncommitted file that content is gone, and the app reports the revert as successful.

escalations.one_line: previewRestore feeds CWD-relative pathspecs to git diff --numstat but joins the paths it returns onto repositoryRoot(), which only holds while git's diff output is repo-root-relative.
criteria: C1: files at the repository root that the turn never touched are deleted outright at Git.swift:619, and uncommitted content in them is not recoverable from the repository.
C4: preview, restore and the app's own report all look normal, so the user gets no signal that the wrong files were acted on and the intended ones left alone.
escalations.worst: A user with diff.relative = true who has added a project that is a subfolder of a larger repository asks to undo a turn's file changes. The files the agent actually changed are not restored at all; the app acts instead on same-named paths at the repository root, DELETING any the base checkpoint does not hold (Git.swift:619) and overwriting any it does (Git.swift:607-611). The revert sheet shows the mis-derived names, which read like plausible file names, and the revert reports success.

register_errors: Entry 2 (AntigravitySession dead mode fields): the dead-store fact is correct but the stated consequence is wrong and must not be propagated. The register says 'A mid-thread mode or Plan/Build change cannot reach agy at all, and even a relaunch uses the original modes while picking up the UPDATED model/effort'. CORRECTION: ThreadRuntime.swift:504-519 includes launchRuntimeMode and launchInteraction in SessionSignature, and :1414/:1418 populate both from thread.* for .antigravity, so the session-reuse check at :1422 fails on any mode or Plan/Build change and :1496-1523 constructs a brand-new AntigravitySession from a fresh SessionConfiguration carrying the CURRENT modes. AntigravitySession is constructed at exactly one site (ThreadRuntime.swift:1516) and start() is only ever called on a freshly made object (:1478, :1486, :1547, :1563), so a relaunch cannot carry stale modes. launchModel and launchEffort are in the signature too, so there is no 'half applied, half discarded' asymmetry. The true finding is a harmless pair of write-only properties. This matters for the port: the Antigravity entries in SessionSignature are what keep the --dangerously-skip-permissions gate (AntigravitySession.swift:135-137) honest, and dropping them would turn this harmless quirk into a real C3/C5 defect that upstream does not have.

Entry 21 (MCPKeychain accessibility never migrates): the description of the code is accurate, but the implied security weakness is not realizable and should not be propagated. CORRECTION: git log -p --follow on DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift shows exactly two commits (739518735 'Add MCP server support', 75e30f217) and kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked is present on the SecItemAdd path in both, so no shipped build ever created these items with a weaker accessibility for the update path to preserve; the macOS default for an add without the attribute is the same value in any case. The observation is true and currently inert. Recorded so the port does not carry it forward as a security finding, and noted that Windows has no kSecAttrAccessible analogue at all since secrets go through DPAPI.

Entry 17 (custom-MCP decode drops every custom server): not wrong, but INCOMPLETE in a way that changes its classification. The register records only the silent drop. It does not record that the drop is followed by an overwrite: customs stays empty and the next saveCustom (MCPStore.swift:175) or deleteCustom (:196) calls saveCustoms, which atomically writes the empty array over mcp-customs.json (:275). That is what takes the defect out of 'no lasting harm' and into C4, and it is why this entry is escalated rather than reproduced. Two smaller citation corrections in the same entry: the tolerance doc comment is at MCPCustom.swift:36-37, not :37-38, and the outer try? is at MCPStore.swift:247, inside the :245-248 load block.

Entry 27: the line cite is wrong. The register cites Hydra.swift:939-940, which is the .stray arm's comment and its 'var parts' line. The .failed arm that omits the pending sentence is at Hydra.swift:936-937. The substance of the entry is correct.

Entry 35: the line range starts one line late. The register cites Hydra.swift:1069-1073; the 'JSON did not parse' nil is at :1068 and the 'every entry was rejected' nil is at :1072. The conflation the entry describes is real.

Entry 39: 'the three deferral exits in startTurn' is loose. There are two enqueueFollowUp call sites inside startTurn (ThreadRuntime.swift:1160 and :1165) covering three conditions (busy, reverting, archived). The entry's own prose names the three conditions, so this is wording rather than a false claim.

Entry 42: 'The comments are wrong' overstates it. Both constants really are 200_000, so 'the same cap' is true of the value; what differs is the operand (Text.swift:101 bounds old.utf8.count + new.utf8.count, ThreadRuntime.swift:3373 bounds the produced diff.utf8.count). It is a misleading true statement, which is why it survives reading.

Entry 44: the stated consequence is wrong. The register says 'a key that had just been promoted out of previous can be dropped at the very next rollover'. It cannot. RecentCache.swift:22-27 promotes the key by re-inserting it, and the write at :54 happens after the rollover block at :47-53, so a just-promoted key always lands in the fresh current, survives the next rollover into previous, and is dropped only at the rollover after that if untouched. The wholesale discard of the older generation is real; the timing claim is off by one generation.

Entry 45: the conclusion is wrong and must not be carried into the port. The register says 'A capture run therefore gets a clean recent-command list but the real machine's model catalogs, contradicting WebsiteCaptures.swift:10-12'. Every UserDefaults.standard site named in the entry is gated on !CaptureRun.isEnabled: ProviderRegistry.swift:162 guards the read at :163, :176 guards the read at :177, :538 guards the write at :541, and :669 guards the write at :672. A capture run therefore neither reads nor writes the real machine's catalogs or catalog dates, and the isolation promised at WebsiteCaptures.swift:10-12 holds. What remains is an inconsistency of mechanism (a separate defaults suite for recentSlashCommands, an outright skip for the catalogs), not a leak.

Entry 50: the entry presents an unreachable branch as a latent trap without saying it is unreachable. ComposerView.swift:1048 defines isVisible as !items.isEmpty, so the switch at :312 cannot be entered with an empty items array, and the clamp at :471 runs only after the non-empty guard at :466-469, so selected is always in range when :321 subscripts. The missing bounds check at :320-322 is real, but it is a dead condition, and the register's suggested Windows no-op changes no reachable behaviour.

Entry 64 cites 'WindowChrome.swift:215-217' for drag(by:). Wrong location: :214-217 is inside the titlebar constraint update loop ('guard changed else { return }' at :214). 'func drag(by translation: CGFloat)' is at :340-342, body 'width = min(Self.maximumWidth, max(0, anchorWidth + translation))'. The rest of entry 64 is correct: endDrag() at :344-356, minimumWidth 210 (:240), maximumWidth 440 (:241), collapseThreshold 110 (:242).
Entry 74 cites 'SettingsView.swift:926-929'. The VStack(spacing: Chrome.sectionSpacing) opens at :927, not :926 (:926 is 'var body: some View {'). Correct span: :927-929. Substance unchanged.

Entry 55 presents LinkParagraphView.dismantleNSView as the complete counterpart to ProseRunView's. Minor imprecision: LinkParagraphView.swift:73-77 clears delegate and mergeTarget and calls streamVeil.detach, but does NOT clear onOpenHead. The asymmetry the entry names (the missing streamVeil.detach in ProseRunView) is real and correctly described.

Entry 62 omits what PopoverItem.confirmation actually is, which invites a wrong reading during the port. Correction for the record: it is an after-the-fact acknowledgement label ('Copied'), documented at Popovers.swift:205-207 as running the action at once, and every use site (RowAction.confirms; TimelineRows.swift:219, :220, :1405, :1406, :1409, :1413) is a Copy or Add. It is NOT a pre-action safety confirmation, so entry 62's synchronous-before-close ordering bypasses no destructive gate and the entry stays ORDINARY. This also means the 'confirmation:' parameter would not have protected entry 68's Delete row even if it had been passed.

Entry 80: the "120 s timeout kill" example does not reach the zip. Shell.terminate (Shell.swift:110-118) leaves a non-zero exit status, so ShellResult.succeeded is false (Shell.swift:9) and the guard at Git.swift:347 returns an empty set before the zip at :350 runs. The one real short-answer-with-exit-0 path is the post-exit drain deadline, Shell.swift:105 `await collector.finished(within: 3)` with OutputCollector.finished at Shell.swift:286-293. The asymmetry the entry records (no count check at :350, a thrown ShellError at :645-646) is correct as written.

Entry 78: two over-statements. A leading ':' can only reach checkoutPaths (Git.swift:395) and removePaths (:400); restore (:609, :617) and blobs (:625) map every path through root.appendingPathComponent(), so their pathspecs always begin with '/' and pathspec magic cannot fire. And previewRestore's own numstat call at :586 also omits --literal-pathspecs, so the revert preview globs exactly as the revert does; the inconsistency is between the diff() helper (:552) and everything else, not between what the user is shown and what is done.

Entry 99: "index.html:547 shows 'Free / AGPL'" is the wrong line. The text is at website/index.html:545 (
FreeAGPL
); line 547 is a system-requirements bullet. The entry's other cites (project.yml:46, pbxproj:295 and :319, LICENSE:4, index.html:766, SettingsView.swift:1003) are exact.

Entry 96: the register says the sibling row at docs/audit-2026-09-15.md:77 drifts in its PATH. It also drifts in its LINE number: Shell.swift:208 is part of the read-only-command classifier, while LoginEnvironment.load, the subject of finding S2, is at Shell.swift:353 and its interactive login shell run is at :369.

Entry 86 (scope, not an error): the entry is right about the algorithm, but repositoryRoot() has only two callers (Git.swift:588 and :603) and both pass the joined paths to blobs() first, whose ls-tree rejects a pathspec outside the repository. A wrong root that lands outside the repository therefore throws before anything is written or deleted, and the revert reports "files could not be restored" (ThreadRuntime.swift:1874-1875). The harm is a failed revert, not a destructive one.

architecture.summary:
Derived the real architecture of the pinned Droppy Code (commit dd2b86ef, tree f761e5ef) into E:/Droppy/port/porting/architecture.md: 967 lines, ten numbered sections covering all eight required topics, with file:line evidence throughout and every claim labelled SOURCE FACT / ENGINEERING DECISION / UNRESOLVED. The reference tree was not modified (git status --porcelain empty, HEAD unchanged).

Measured shape (counted, not estimated): 191 Swift files, 72,303 Swift lines under DroppyCode/, split App 78/40,860, Services 49/16,759, UI 34/8,854, Core 30/5,830, plus 2 Objective-C implementations, 1 bridging header and 1 Metal shader. Single Swift module (project.yml syncedFolder, PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME DroppyCode), one third-party package (SwiftTerm exactVersion 1.20.0), macOS 26.0 / Swift 6.0 / arm64 only.

The AGENTS.md four-layer rule was tested mechanically (939 declared type names mapped to layers, every non-comment line of Core/Services/UI scanned, 29 candidates hand-verified at their cited lines, 24 false positives from string literals and generic parameter names discarded). It is VIOLATED: Core is not dependency-free and UI is not Core-only. The rule is also unenforceable, since all four directories compile into one Swift module with no build check.

Lifecycle is documented in the real order with the source's own stated reasons: DroppyCodeApp.init's five ordered side effects (notification-guard swizzle before any post, SIGPIPE ignore, WebsiteCaptures.prepare before any settings or library read, LegacyMigration, HangWatchdog + SwitchLatency); AppModel.init's nine steps including the MCPStore constructor that binds a loopback listener and rewrites every provider config file; applicationDidFinishLaunching's nine steps including the capture-run early return; AppKit window construction (the app has NO SwiftUI windows, the Scene is Settings { EmptyView() } carrying only menus); bootstrap's nine ordered awaits; the quit path's 240 s Hydra merge wait at 250 ms polls; and applicationWillTerminate's three calls with the teardown gaps that are real and must be reproduced (MCPProbe children and provider StdioProcess children are not in the tracked process set; MCPProxy and WorkingTreeWatch are never torn down).

Three corrections to prior port records were made from the source: AppSettings.Key has 61 constants (not 78); Git.swift has exactly 18 explicit-timeout sites, all 300 s, split 12 git and 6 forge, which confirms STATE.md's correction and contradicts the git-command-vectors extract's "thirteen"; and the layering claim in porting/CLAUDE.md ("confirmed against the tree") is wrong.

UNK-0010 is recorded in section 9 as explicitly unresolved and isolated. No behaviour is chosen, neither alternative is treated as approved, and the document is written so that nothing else depends on its outcome. Section 9 also restates that the 99-defect record is not blanket approval for destructive or security-sensitive behaviour.

This is specification work only. No Windows functionality was implemented or tested in this task.
layering_violations: Core -> Services: Core/Models/MCP.swift:165 calls MCPProxy.url(for: id) to build an OAuth server's URL. MCPProxy is declared at Services/MCP/MCPProxy.swift:5. AGENTS.md:15-16 says Core reaches into nothing else in the app.

Core -> Services: Core/Models/MCP.swift:238, :244 and :246 compute MCPPaths.directory, MCPPaths.connectionsURL and MCPPaths.customsURL from Storage.root, declared at Services/Store/Storage.swift:18. MCPPaths.directory is a static let whose initializer creates the directory as a side effect, so the coupling also fixes WHEN that directory appears on disk.

UI -> App: UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:75 reads WebsiteCaptures.defaults (`private let defaults = WebsiteCaptures.defaults ?? .standard`). WebsiteCaptures is declared at App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift:21. AGENTS.md:16-18 says UI reaches only into Core.
UI -> Services: UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift:89, :128 and :130 use Storage.wallpaperDirectory, declared at Services/Store/Storage.swift:18.

UI -> App: UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift:331 instantiates HydraDelegationBlock(json: code, sent: info != "hydra"), a view declared at App/Views/Chat/TimelineRows.swift:652. This makes the markdown renderer depend on the chat feature views and therefore not reusable in isolation.

Structural finding, not a per-site violation: the rule is unenforceable. project.yml:19-21 puts DroppyCode as a single syncedFolder into one target with PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME DroppyCode, so all four 'layers' compile into one Swift module with no module boundary, no access-control barrier and no build check. AGENTS.md:26-28 states 'the build is the check', and the build cannot check this.
Related finding: Core is not even UI-framework-free. Core has 3 `import SwiftUI` and 1 `import AppKit`, and Core/Models/MCP.swift:255 declares `extension Color`.

Not a violation but the most load-bearing structural fact: AppModel and ThreadRuntime are mutually dependent inside the App layer. AppModel owns runtimes strongly (AppModel.swift:108) and ThreadRuntime holds `private weak var app: AppModel?` (ThreadRuntime.swift:413). The weak direction must be preserved.
architecture.concurrency_model:
Main-actor confinement is the primary model and it is a correctness invariant, not a style choice. Counted from source: 256 @MainActor annotations across 89 files, 99 nonisolated, 40 @Observable, 158 Sendable conformances, 24 Task.detached, 11 MainActor.assumeIsolated, 9 MainActor.run.

Every stateful application object is main-actor confined: AppModel (AppModel.swift:12), ThreadRuntime (ThreadRuntime.swift:166), TimelineEntry (:6), AppSettings (AppSettings.swift:110), ProviderRegistry (ProviderRegistry.swift:30), MCPStore (MCPStore.swift:8), TerminalStore and TerminalSession (TerminalStore.swift:5, :103), TokenLedger (TokenLedger.swift:61), WindowManager (WindowManager.swift:9), AppDelegate (AppDelegate.swift:4), WindowLiveResize (WindowManager.swift:118). TokenLedger.swift:105-106 states the invariant as its correctness argument: "Every provider session runs on the main actor, so this needs no lock." Every provider adapter's onEvent callback therefore lands on the main actor. A Windows stack that splits UI and logic across threads or processes must either preserve this or add the missing locks.

Actors: exactly two in the whole tree. Core/Support/ThumbnailCache.swift:9 and Services/MCP/MCPHub.swift:17 (MCPHub.shared at :18). MCPHub deliberately punches two nonisolated static holes through its own isolation (track(_:) at :25, terminateAll() at :29) because applicationWillTerminate cannot await an actor hop.

@concurrent: 16 sites, complete list. ThreadRuntime.swift:2018, :2023, :3381; ComposerView.swift:1161, :1185, :1256; Timeline.swift:99; Shell.swift:35, :363; MCPProbe.swift:52; NativeFileTools.swift:40, :79, :92, :122; OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:595; MarkdownView.swift:237. The two that matter structurally: Shell.run is @concurrent (Shell.swift:35), so every process the app launches is launched off the main actor, and LoginEnvironment.read() likewise (:363).

Detached work: DocumentPrefetch's single utility worker (Storage.swift:293) and Storage.sweepOrphanedAttachments (Storage.swift:120) are the structurally important ones.

Locks and queues, full inventory in section 5.5: 3 Mutex in Shell.swift (:326 login environment, :329 single-flight load task, :398 resolved git binary); NSLock at Shell.swift:220 (OnceContinuation) and :250 (OutputCollector); OSAllocatedUnfairLock at HangWatchdog.swift:34; NSLock + DispatchQueue("droppycode.stdio.write") at StdioProcess.swift:20-21; Mutex at Git.swift:509 and WorkingTreeWatch.swift:86 with DispatchQueue("droppy.working-tree-watch") at :121; two NSLock in MCPHub.swift (:499 HubConversation, :534 MCPLiveProcesses); two NSLock in MCPOAuth.swift (:82, :101) plus DispatchQueue("MCPOAuth.callback") at :420; NSLock at MCPProbe.swift:384; Mutex<UInt16> + NSLock + DispatchQueue("MCPProxy") at MCPProxy.swift:14, :53-54; Mutex<State> at Storage.swift:260; DispatchQueue("droppycode.storage.write", .utility) + Mutex at Storage.swift:339, :343; NSLock at AppUpdater.swift:459 and LinkTitles.swift:84; DispatchQueue("droppycode.website-captures.film", .userInteractive) at WebsiteCaptures.swift:1064.

Ten places where ordering is load-bearing (section 5.6): (1) DroppyCodeApp.init's five-step launch order, notification guard before any post and WebsiteCaptures.prepare before any settings or library read; (2) releaseSession resets sessionEpoch, sessionSignature, unsentSessionID, antiSlopFallbackSent and continuationSent BEFORE its `guard let old = session` (ThreadRuntime.swift:2042-2052), so they reset even with no session, and onEvent is cleared one runloop turn later on purpose because a closing session usually speaks from inside its own handler; (3) flushDeltas() runs before every completion handler or text is lost; (4) finishingTurnID is claimed before the first await in finishTurn, which is what makes .turnCompleted + .exited idempotent; (5) unsentSessionID is consumed only after a successful send (:1315-1318) and discarded by a release, while the API-key branch bypasses it entirely and writes providerSessionID directly at :1490; (6) AppModel's sync/write split (AppModel.swift:157-182) defers cell writes out of the dictionary's exclusive-access scope because a cell write inside withAnimation makes SwiftUI rebuild the menu commands synchronously and re-enter thread(_:); (7) bootstrap runs LoginEnvironment.load() before sweepHydraCopies() so git gets the user's PATH; (8) saveNow cancels its timer first, since a standing handle would suppress every later save until the turn ended; (9) MCP HTTP per-server headers are applied first and then overwritten by the fixed Content-Type, Accept and MCP-Protocol-Version; (10) MCPHub.terminateAll SIGTERMs all, then SIGKILLs all still running, with no sleep between the loops.
architecture.lifecycle:
Process start (DroppyCodeApp.swift:3-19), five side effects in this exact order, each with a source comment giving the reason: 1) DCInstallNotificationGuard() swizzles NSNotificationCenter's two posting methods to catch an observer exception (DCNotificationGuard.m:19-40), and must run before anything posts; 2) signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) so a write to an exited provider child returns EPIPE instead of killing the process; 3) WebsiteCaptures.prepare() before anything reads settings or the library (a no-op in a normal launch; in a capture run it wipes the capture storage root, recreates threads/ and films/, removes the persistent domain iordv.droppycode.website-captures and writes a fixed fixture library); 4) LegacyMigration.run() (one-time carry from bundle id iordv.cody and the Application Support folder Cody, LegacyMigration.swift:5-25); 5) HangWatchdog.start() then SwitchLatency.start().

The Scene is Settings { EmptyView() }.commands { AppCommands(model: WindowManager.shared.model) } (DroppyCodeApp.swift:21-25). The app has NO SwiftUI windows. Reading WindowManager.shared here is what constructs WindowManager and with it AppModel, a stored let at WindowManager.swift:13.

AppModel.init (AppModel.swift:120-146), nine steps: AppSettings() reads every default; ProviderRegistry(settings:); MCPStore() which calls load(), then MCPProxy.shared.start() binding a loopback TCP listener, then exportAll() rewriting every provider MCP config file (MCPStore.swift:22-28); TerminalStore(); SidebarLayout(); Storage.loadLibrary() synchronously reading and decoding library.json (Storage.swift:60-63); crash recovery in two loops (lastStatus .running becomes .interrupted at :129-131, hydra?.status .running becomes .stopped with finishedAt = .now at :133-136); observation cells built by hand because property observers stay quiet inside an initializer (:137-141); AutoContinue(app: self); and a dangling settings.lastProjectID cleared (:143-145).

applicationDidFinishLaunching (AppDelegate.swift:8-28), in order: notification centre delegate; WindowManager.shared and model captured; capture-run fork that returns early and never shows the main window, never bootstraps and never checks for updates; windows.showMain(); openThreadOnLaunch() (AppModel.swift:574-601, reuses the newest unused untitled unsent non-helper thread in the current project, re-stamping provider/model/effort/fastMode/hydraPairID from a fresh thread and clearing providerSessionID and providerResumeAt if the provider changed, else newThread(in:)); the tour after a literal 700 ms sleep if !settings.hasSeenTour; Task { await model.bootstrap() }; UpdateChecker.shared.startBackgroundChecks() (8 s launch delay, 6 h interval, UpdateChecker.swift:74-75); and the post-install relaunch marker which arms the celebration and opens Settings on About.

Window construction (WindowManager.swift:62-110): plain AppKit windows. Class DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow by default, ThreadWindow for main, SecondaryWindow for settings. Style mask [.titled, .closable, .miniaturizable, .fullSizeContentView] plus .resizable when resizable. isReleasedWhenClosed = false, animationBehavior = .documentWindow, tabbingMode = .disallowed, then WindowChrome.configure(window). Content is a WindowLiveResize observer plus FrameHostingView(rootView: AnyView(HostedRoot(...))) inside a plain NSView container. Main 1320x860, minimum 860x560, settings 780x580. Frame autosave name "DroppyCodeMainWindow". FrameHostingView always accepts first responder (:211) and returns false from performKeyEquivalent while hidden (:216-218).

Bootstrap (AppModel.swift:239-278), nine ordered steps: warmDocuments of the 12 most recently updated non-archived non-panel threads; await settings.loadKeychainInBackground(); await LoginEnvironment.load() (everything after runs with the user's PATH); sweepHydraCopies(); await resumeHydraMerges() (the launch merge sweep); hydraMergeSweepTask started as a loop sleeping .seconds(300) for the life of the app; await providers.refreshAll(); a withTaskGroup loading catalogs for [.claude, .codex, .deepseek, .meta] that report installed, then .zai serially; and finally, guarded by !WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, await Storage.sweepOrphanedAttachments().

Steady state: three regimes. The main actor runs the whole UI, AppModel, every ThreadRuntime, AppSettings, ProviderRegistry, MCPStore, TerminalStore and TokenLedger. Private serial queues run disk writes, stdio writes, the MCP proxy, FSEvents and (in capture runs) film encoding. Detached tasks run document decoding, shell processes and the attachment sweep. Two lifelong timers: Hydra merge sweep every 300 s, update check every 6 h. Per backgrounded thread, scheduleIdleSessionStop runs a 600 s loop (AppModel.swift:476-487) that stops the session and releases the runtime when it holds only persisted state.

Quit, applicationShouldTerminate (AppDelegate.swift:38-48): returns .terminateNow unless model.isAnyHydraMergeRunning; otherwise polls every 250 ms against a deadline of Date.now + 4 * 60 seconds and then replies true, returning .terminateLater. isAnyHydraMergeRunning is liveRuntimes.contains { $0.isHydraMerging } (AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:31) and liveRuntimes is Array(runtimes.values) (AppModel.swift:437), so a merge owned by a runtime that was released for idleness would not be seen; in practice the merge holds its runtime, so the window is narrow, but it is a real property of the design.

Terminate cleanup, applicationWillTerminate (AppDelegate.swift:50-55): exactly three calls, model?.saveBeforeQuit(), TokenLedger.shared.flushLiveSpend(), MCPHub.terminateAll(). saveBeforeQuit (AppModel.swift:1309-1327) latches persistenceEnabled = false so nothing can queue another save, cancels saveTask, writes the Library synchronously, then per live runtime cancelPersistence() + stopSession() + writeSynchronously only when unsavedSnapshot() is non-nil, then DiskWriter.waitForQueuedWrites() (a queue.sync {} barrier), then terminals.terminateAll(). MCPHub.terminateAll (MCPHub.swift:196-205) SIGTERMs every tracked server then SIGKILLs the process group of any still running.

Teardown gaps that are real and must be reproduced, not fixed: MCPHub.track(_:) is called from exactly one site (MCPHub.swift:370), so MCPProbe's children (MCPProbe.swift:121) and every provider StdioProcess child (StdioProcess.swift:16) are not in the tracked set; provider children are only stopped indirectly through stopSession() for runtimes still alive. MCPProxy is never stopped. WorkingTreeWatch's FSEvents streams and their scratch index files in the temporary directory are not torn down.
port_critical: Liquid Glass is the app's entire surface and it is macOS-delegated. 22 glassEffect/GlassEffectContainer sites across 18 files (Chrome.swift:178, :180, :243, :252 plus 17 feature views), and one Metal shader used through SwiftUI's .distortionEffect(ShaderLibrary.genie(...)) at Genie.swift:157-158 with Genie.metal. Chrome.swift:219 records the measured cost: a window-sized glass surface is a full-window backdrop sample every frame. Under OD-0003 a stack that cannot render a custom material with backdrop sampling, blur, specular edge and interactive response is disqualified. This is the single largest constraint.

The windows are AppKit, not SwiftUI scenes. WindowManager.swift:62-110 builds NSWindows directly; the app's only Scene is Settings { EmptyView() } carrying menus. Frame autosave, fullSizeContentView, two Objective-C NSWindow subclasses for macOS-specific crashes, a hosting view that always accepts first responder and suppresses key equivalents while hidden, and traffic-light-derived layout constants (Chrome.trafficLightTop, Chrome.trafficLightDiameter, read at RootView.swift:30 and :62) that have no Windows analogue and must be re-derived as a recorded deviation.

Main-actor confinement is a correctness invariant. 256 @MainActor annotations, exactly two actors, and TokenLedger.swift:105-106 explicitly skips locking on the strength of it. Any stack with a different UI thread model must reintroduce by hand the ten ordering rules in section 5.6, of which sessionEpoch, finishingTurnID and unsentSessionID are the most likely to break.

Subprocess control is deep and POSIX-shaped: SIGPIPE ignored process-wide, SIGTERM then SIGKILL with a one-second gap, process-group kill conditioned on getpgid(pid) == pid (Shell.swift:116, MCPHub.swift:203, and neither site calls setsid so whether the group dies depends on the child), a pty for the terminal panel via SwiftTerm, a login shell run with -l -i -c to harvest the environment, /usr/bin/env -0 NUL parsing, and a colon-separated PATH. UNK-0005 (what shell runs model-issued commands on Windows) and UNK-0006 (Command Code's executable is literally `cmd`, colliding with the Windows interpreter) both live here and block PA-0009 and PA-0011.

Shell command write-classification is product behaviour, not plumbing (Shell.swift:136-216). Whether a model-issued command counts as a reader decides whether a working-tree snapshot is taken around it, which decides what the timeline's changes row shows. The table is 52 tool names plus 25 git subcommands (both counts re-verified from source), with special cases for sort, xcodebuild, env and the version-flag tools. It is a table of Unix tool names.

FSEvents has no Windows equivalent with the same semantics. WorkingTreeWatch uses kFSEventStreamCreateFlagFileEvents | kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer, resolves paths with realpath(3) because events name /private/var, writes cookie files under the git directory to order events, keeps a scratch git index per watch, and caps the registry at 32. ReadDirectoryChangesW differs in coalescing, path form and overflow.

Two separate Keychain surfaces with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked, both keyed by service AppInfo.name: provider API keys in AppSettings.swift:356-395 and MCP field values in MCPKeychain.swift:30-50. Both retain a UserDefaults fallback for migration. A Windows replacement must be equally per-user and equally unavailable while locked, and the fallback must not silently become the normal path.

Iconography and type are macOS-supplied and non-redistributable: 181 Image(systemName:) sites. SF Symbols and the macOS system font cannot ship on Windows, and text metrics feed layout, so substitution is a measured change (UNK-0007, PA-0012, PA-0013).

Single-module compilation hides the layering. Because all four directories are one Swift module with five confirmed upward references, a Windows solution that splits Core/Services/UI/App into separate assemblies or crates will not compile a faithful transcription without seams at Core/Models/MCP.swift, UI/Theme/Wallpaper.swift and UI/Markdown/MarkdownView.swift. Decide before the first project file is written.

Storage is two roots, not one (Storage.swift:19-48): ~/Library/Application Support/<name>/ for library, threads, attachments, wallpaper and MCP, and ~/.droppy-code/ (or .droppy-code-dev) for worktrees and patches. The split must be kept because git worktree records absolute paths.

The update feed ports, the install path does not. UpdateChecker reads the public GitLab Releases API with no token (project id 86415974, per_page=20, UpdateChecker.swift:66-70) and is platform-neutral. AppUpdater mounts a .dmg with hdiutil, copies with ditto, verifies the signature and writes a detached shell script that waits for the app to quit, swaps the bundle and relaunches (AppUpdater.swift:286-415). UNK-0009 keeps the live update path BLOCKED rather than faked.

Timings are specified, not emergent. The port must hit literals: flush window 45 ms; flush tiers 45/90/150 ms at 4,096 and 32,768 characters; scrolling floor 160 ms; head flush floor max(45, streamingCount * 70) ms; idle save 800 ms; running save 5 s; library save 400 ms; interrupt watchdog 8 s; finish-turn grace 3 s; idle session stop 600 s; Hydra merge sweep 300 s; quit merge wait 240 s at 250 ms polls; update launch delay 8 s, interval 6 h; git 120 s default with 300 s at 18 sites (12 git, 6 forge); MCP 60 s initialize, 60 s tools/list, 120 s tools/call, 90 s probe (240 s with mcp-remote), 3,600 s proxy upstream; shell output grace 3 s; process kill gap 1 s.

Shipped-but-dead state must be reproduced as dead. TurnRecord.tokenSpends is declared (Timeline.swift:269), decoded (:292) and read once (HydraRunMetricsView.swift:135) but never assigned anywhere in the repository, so the Hydra run-metrics view always renders empty for spends. 60 such items are recorded with proof in porting/dead_code.md.

UNRESOLVED and blocking the provider layer: the pinned checkout does not compile. Four session adapters emit onEvent?(.tokenSpend(...)) (AntigravitySession.swift:308, CommandCodeSession.swift:350, CopilotSession.swift:554, OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:494) while enum ProviderEvent at this commit has 30 cases and no tokenSpend (ProviderSession.swift:82-118). The commit is mid-refactor. Port the 30-case enum as committed, or the 31-case enum the adapters expect. Recorded, not guessed.

UNK-0010 is carried as explicitly unresolved and isolated in section 9: deleting a custom MCP server runs on one click with no confirmation (MCPSettingsPage.swift:564-566) and also deletes the server's Keychain secrets (MCPStore.swift:193-199 to disconnect to MCPKeychain.deleteAll at MCPStore.swift:124), ignoring confirmBeforeDeleting which defaults true (AppSettings.swift:702) and is honoured by six other destructive paths (SettingsView.swift:851, :892; SidebarView.swift:192, :360, :891). No behaviour chosen, neither alternative approved, and nothing else in the specification depends on the outcome.
